items.title: The Republicans Are Bolting From Trump
items.description: A few tentative displays of independence among Republicans have expanded in recent days into a stampede, as candidates furiously distance themselves from President Trump ahead of the midterm elections. “This is shaping up to be a nightmare political environment for every Republican, everywhere—period, full stop,” one Texas-based political consultant told us, speaking anonymously to provide a frank assessment. Noting that gas prices across the country are on average $4.50 a gallon, the consultant described the atmosphere as “a fucking disaster for anyone in a competitive race.” The contrast with the midterm elections of Trump’s first term is particularly stark. An October 2018 rally in Richmond, Kentucky, was a political show of force by a president whose hold on the Republican Party was as firm as bedrock. The opening speaker, Republican State Senator Ralph Alvarado, hailed Trump’s many accomplishments as “amazing to see.” Senator Rand Paul crowed that Trump “exceeds my expectations” almost every day. Representative Andy Barr, whom Trump had come to town to endorse, praised the president as “a man of action” who “gets results,” prompting the thousands of MAGA faithful in attendance to erupt in cheers. Kentucky Republicans have been fawning over Trump for the past decade. But now, as the war with Iran drags on and Trump’s approval ratings crater, even they are starting to keep the president at a distance. Barr, who is running for an open Senate seat, and Alvarado, who is running to replace him in the House, have each recently scrubbed mentions of Trump’s name from prominent portions of their campaign websites. Paul has been more vocal, repeatedly clashing with the White House over the Iran war and the ballooning national debt. The notably lukewarm embrace of Trump from Republican candidates in Kentucky, a state that he won by more than 30 points in 2024, is just one indicator of the president’s loosening grip on a party he has dominated for the past decade. Republican candidates seeking a reason to distance themselves from an unpopular president have a buffet of options to choose from. The war in Iran, which began almost seven months ago, has sent diesel prices to record highs. The United States is in an escalating trade war with Canada. The national debt, the elimination of which was once an obsession of conservatives, has ballooned to more than $40 trillion—and that’s before the $5,000 government checks Trump has promised to dole out if Republicans win. Inflation and interest rates, which Trump pledged to bring down, remain elevated. Gas and food are more expensive than they were a year ago, and mortgage rates passed 7 percent yesterday. The president’s approval ratings on these and other issues are abysmal. A Reuters/Ipsos poll released Monday found that his approval rating has dipped to 32 percent—the lowest that pollster has measured at any point in his political career. Only 17 percent of respondents said they approved of the president’s handling of the cost of living. Barring a major change in the Iran war or the price of diesel, his numbers aren’t likely to change substantially, the Texas-based Republican consultant said. Members of his party were hoping the dynamic would improve, but it hasn’t—giving them little choice but to scramble over one another for the emergency exits. The list of Republican candidates publicly noting their differences with Trump keeps growing. Many are in states where polls show tighter-than-expected races for the GOP. Senator Roger Marshall of Kansas spoke out this month about Trump’s calls to ban the sale of jets from the Canadian company Bombardier, whose U.S. headquarters are in Wichita. The Senate candidates Mike Rogers in Michigan, Ashley Hinson in Iowa, and Jon Husted in Ohio have each called for a swift end to the war in Iran, noting its impact on gas prices even as Trump has claimed that such hikes are “a very inexpensive price to pay for what we’ve done” there. Even in Trump’s adopted state of Florida, which he’s won three times, candidates are bailing. Representative Byron Donalds, who is running for governor, recently updated his campaign website to remove multiple references to Trump—including a photo with the president and a banner noting that he was “TRUMP-ENDORSED,” the Miami Herald reported Tuesday. Last week, Representative María Elvira Salazar released a political ad filmed in front of the White House warning the president that Hispanic voters “feel betrayed” by immigration and deportation policies that have “gone too far.” Marshall, the Kansas senator who has been a vocal supporter of Trump’s immigration crackdowns, shifted his tone this week, asserting that ICE agents conducting raids in his state needed to “coordinate with our local law enforcement.” Even red-state Republicans who are not on the ballot are seeking daylight between themselves and the president. Senator John Curtis of Utah this week called for an investigation into Trump’s son Don Jr. over corruption allegations, including concerns about a luxurious, days-long party for his wedding that was funded by a Russian oligarch . Senator Roger Wicker of Mississippi on Wednesday took to the Senate floor to admonish the White House for giving “brutal” Chinese President Xi Jinping a “lavish welcome” to the U.S. this week. [ Read: The deferential president ] “The midterms are going to be a fucking bloodbath, and we all know it and we all know why,” Representative Nancy Mace, a retiring South Carolina Republican, told us of the president she once enthusiastically supported. She broke with him earlier this year and last week voted to end the Iran war. “We haven’t done what we said we were going to do, and Republicans are the least motivated group to turn out this cycle.” T rump is not the first president to see members of his party running in the opposite direction in an attempt to salvage their political fortunes. Barack Obama and George W. Bush each steered clear of certain vulnerable members’ districts ahead of challenging midterm elections. Joe Biden, who faced sinking approval ratings during the 2022 midterms, regularly said he would happily campaign with or against any Democrat, if doing so would help them get elected. But only Trump has demanded extreme loyalty. Stepping out of line was a rarity during the first year and a half of Trump’s second term, which began with a flurry of executive actions that left much of Washington shell-shocked. But Trump could demand fealty for only so long, Russell Riley, a presidential historian at the University of Virginia’s Miller Center, told us. “The cascading opposition to the president on multiple fronts now is important not just because of what it might represent for the midterm election, but more so because it reestablishes a kind of fixed point of orientation in the political universe again, making it possible for those who were persistently disoriented to regain their balance,” he said. Even as the evidence has mounted that Trump is dragging down his party, the president has highlighted the very positions that have made him unpopular. After it was already clear that public concern over data centers was endangering the campaigns of vulnerable Republicans such as Husted, Trump insulted communities that rejected the projects as places that wanted to end up “backwards and poor.” He has dismissed bipartisan efforts to rein in the dangers of AI, saying he wants technology companies to have freedom to develop what he has begun referring to as “super intelligence.” He has continued to defend the war in Iran—suggesting this week at the United Nations that he might annihilate the entire country—and minimized the economic cost Americans are shouldering as a result. Trump has also repeatedly told voters to pretend that he was on the ballot. Democrats have been happy to oblige, mentioning the president in 66,000 airings of general-election ads since August 1, according to the political-ad tracking firm AdImpact. (Republicans have mentioned Trump in a mere 7,000 airings.) The president does still have sway over his most die-hard supporters, and the White House provided us with a lengthy list of Republicans who continue to campaign with the president and praise him on social media and in speeches. He is also still deploying the enormous resources of political action committees he controls to help the GOP. “President Trump is the unequivocal leader, best messenger, and unmatched motivator for the Republican Party, and he is committed to maintaining Republican majorities in Congress,” the White House spokesperson Davis Ingle told us in a statement. “The choice has never been more clear: doubling down on President Trump’s winning, commonsense agenda or the Democrats’ extreme liberal policies and obstruction.” The campaigns of Salazar, Donalds, Alvarado, Barr, Rogers, and Hinson did not respond to our requests for comment. (Salazar has said that she met with Trump after her ad went up and had a cordial conversation about immigration.) Dozens of Republicans broke with Trump after the January 6 insurrection, only for many to return to the fold after he won office a second time. But for those who have been eager to see the party move on from Trump, the events of the past few weeks mark a potentially more durable shift. Mike Madrid, a Republican strategist and co-founder of the anti-Trump Lincoln Project, told us he has been watching the MAGA movement for a decade, asking: “When is this fever swamp gonna finally break?” He thinks the moment is now. Candidates have begun making the calculation that Trump is more of a liability than an asset, and are de-emphasizing their relationship with him. “This is the first time I’ve ever seen that,” he said. The fact that it’s happening even in places like Kentucky is telling. In May, Trump successfully intervened in a House primary in the state to punish Thomas Massie for breaking ranks. But things are now very different. Barr, who is widely expected to win the Senate race in November, removed a photo of himself with Trump from the front page of his website and changed the phrase “America First” to “Kentucky First.” (The website still features language describing Barr as the first member of the state’s congressional delegation to endorse Trump.) The campaign website for Alvarado, who is running in the state’s most competitive congressional district, also scrubbed a photo with Trump and replaced multiple references to the president’s name. When asked about candidates such as Hinson and Rogers publicly calling for an end to the war in Iran, a Republican operative told us that they were “not running away from Trump in his entirety” but instead making specific distinctions while still embracing the president’s broader record. Trump has not lashed out against candidates who are moving away from him. That’s a shift from years past, and his decision to hold his fire may be giving more candidates confidence to pull away. “It’s more that they’re allowed to have disagreements on certain issues with Trump,” the operative, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, said. Trump has also distanced himself from some Republicans, at least the ones not polling very well. Last month, he told Punchbowl News that voters were “not angry at me, but they are angry at Republicans.” He has repeatedly noted that GOP turnout tends to drop when he is not on the ballot, saying that he viewed such political trends as a kind of personal compliment despite their detrimental consequences for members of his party. [ Read: An electoral mess in Missouri ] The day after the 2018 midterms, when Republicans lost 40 seats in the House, Trump held a press conference and singled out the losing Republican candidates who had rejected his “embrace” during the campaign. “You had some that decided to ‘Let’s stay away, let’s stay away.’ They did very poorly,” he told reporters. “I’m not sure that I should be happy or sad, but I feel just fine about it.” He then went on to mockingly name a handful of the defeated candidates. It is easy to imagine the president holding a similar news conference this fall, calling out the Republicans who kept him away during the campaign. This time, the list would be much longer.

Attaques terroristes au Sahel : le Chef de la diplomatie burkinabè déplore une « caution inavouée » de la communauté internationale
items.description: Le Camarade ministre des Affaires étrangères, Karamoko Jean Marie TRAORE, a rencontré Monsieur Alexandre ZOUEV, Sous-Secrétaire général par intérim du Bureau des Nations Unies de lutte contre le terrorisme, le 25 septembre 2026. Cette rencontre a été une opportunité pour les deux hommes, de passer en revue le partenariat et de faire des suggestions pour améliorer ce partenariat entre le Burkina Faso et cette entité onusienne, qui apporte un soutien à notre pays dans la lutte contre le terrorisme, à travers notamment le renforcement des capacités opérationnelles des acteurs chargés de cette lutte. Le responsable onusien a réitéré l’engagement de sa structure à poursuivre l'appui au Burkina Faso, en matière d'enquêtes anti terroristes et d'autres programmes de collaboration. Le ministre des Affaires étrangères a indiqué que le Burkina Faso apprécie la collaboration avec le Bureau des Nations Unies pour la lutte contre le terrorisme. Mais tirant leçon de ce qui n'a pas marché jusque-là, il a souligné la nécessité de mettre l'accent sur le volet prévention pour éviter les recrutements des jeunes dans les rangs des terroristes, et de rallier plusieurs autres acteurs pour aller dans une démarche plus globale dans cette lutte. A cette audience, le Chef de la diplomatie burkinabè a exprimé son indignation face à la caution non avoué que la communauté internationale accorde aux groupes terroristes, soit à travers le silence soit à travers l'offre d'espaces d'expression à ces groupes. A titre d'exemple, le ministre des Affaires étrangères est revenu sur la surprise des pays de la Confédération AES, de constater le silence totale de la communauté internationale lorsque le JNIM s'est associé à un groupe séparatiste (le FLA) pour attaquer le Mali en avril dernier. >, a déclaré le ministre Karamoko Jean Marie TRAORE. items.title: Pape Léon XIV en France: quatre jours de visite entre paix, dialogue et spiritualité
items.description: Le pape Léon XIV a entamé, ce vendredi 25 septembre 2026, une visite apostolique de quatre jours en France. Arrivé à Paris dans la matinée, le souverain pontife doit se rendre successivement à Paris, Saint-Denis, Lourdes et Metz, avec un programme mêlant rencontres politiques, plaidoyer pour la paix, échanges avec la jeunesse et temps forts religieux. Après 18 ans sans visite d’un pape à Paris, depuis le déplacement de Benoît XVI en 2008, l’arrivée de Léon XIV en France constitue un événement particulièrement attendu. Le souverain pontife a atterri vendredi matin à l’aéroport de Paris-Orly, donnant le coup d’envoi d’un séjour prévu jusqu’au 28 septembre. À 10h, heure de Paris, les cloches des églises de France ont résonné simultanément pour saluer son arrivée, rapporte LeMonde. Une première journée entre Élysée et UNESCO Le pape Léon XIV a débuté sa journée à l’Élysée, où il a été reçu par le président Emmanuel Macron. Les deux hommes ont échangé avant que le souverain pontife ne prononce un discours en français devant les autorités françaises et le corps diplomatique. Cette première séquence a, notamment, été placée sous le signe de la paix et de la dignité humaine, avec pour devise: «Pour que le monde ait la vie», indique Vatican News. Dans l’après-midi, le pape s’est rendu au siège de l’UNESCO à Paris, à l’invitation de son directeur général. Il y a défendu l’importance de l’éducation, de la paix et du dialogue éthique, notamment face aux bouleversements liés au développement de l’intelligence artificielle. Notre-Dame, avant une soirée avec la jeunesse En fin d’après-midi, Léon XIV doit poursuivre son programme avec une déambulation en papamobile dans la capitale, avant de rejoindre Notre-Dame de Paris pour la célébration des vêpres (prière traditionnelle du soir dans la tradition chrétienne. Le Vatican a mis l’accent sur le caractère avant tout spirituel de cette étape dans la cathédrale restaurée, privilégiant un temps de prière avec les prêtres plutôt qu’une succession d’apparitions à caractère politique. La première journée doit s’achever à Saint-Denis, avec une grande veillée organisée au Stade de France en présence de jeunes. De Paris à Lourdes puis Metz Le programme se poursuivra samedi 26 septembre avec des rencontres associatives et universitaires à Paris. Le pape participera ensuite à une messe en plein air sur la place de la Concorde, avant de prendre la direction de Lourdes. Dimanche 27 septembre sera consacré au sanctuaire de Lourdes, où Léon XIV doit notamment rencontrer des malades. Une rencontre privée avec des victimes de violences sexuelles au sein de l’Église est également prévue. La dernière étape de cette visite aura lieu lundi 28 septembre à Metz. Cette séquence doit notamment être consacrée à une ouverture vers l’Europe, avant le retour du souverain pontife à Rome. Pendant quatre jours, le déplacement de Léon XIV en France combine ainsi rencontres institutionnelles, dialogue autour des grands enjeux contemporains, échanges avec la jeunesse et étapes spirituelles, dans un voyage placé sous le signe de la paix et de la dignité humaine. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Pape Léon XIV en France: quatre jours de visite entre paix, dialogue et spiritualité est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: 64 arrested over alleged unlawful possession of firearms at Achimota lounge
items.description: The Office of the Special Operations Assistant to the Inspector-General of Police (SOA), in collaboration with the National SWAT, has arrested 64 suspects in an operation targeting alleged unlawful possession of firearms and ammunition at a lounge near Achimota Mile 7 in the Greater Accra Region. According to a post shared on Facebook on Friday, September 25, the operation followed complaints from residents about suspected criminal activities at the lounge and its surrounding areas, including the alleged open display and possible trading of firearms. According to the Police, officers identified a blue, unregistered Acura vehicle during the operation and found a pistol holster inside. The vehicle was impounded and conveyed to the Police Headquarters for further investigations after no person at the scene claimed ownership of the holster. The Police said one of the suspects, Theophilus Ashon, claimed to be a police officer attached to the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) Operations. However, checks conducted by the Police established that he was not a member of the Ghana Police Service. A search of Ashon allegedly led to the recovery of a Smith & Wesson pistol loaded with six rounds of 9mm ammunition. Further investigations subsequently led officers to Atico, where another suspect, Michael Emmanuel Kingsley Mills, was arrested. A search of Mills’ residence resulted in the recovery of three pump-action guns, four pistols, 62 AA and BB cartridges, and 54 rounds of .40-calibre ammunition, alongside other exhibits. The 64 suspects are currently in Police custody assisting with investigations and are expected to be put before the court. The Police have also urged residents to continue providing information on suspected criminal activities to assist law enforcement agencies in maintaining public safety and security.

items.title: Savannah Regional Minister calls for clear rules to distinguish generosity from vote-buying
items.description: Savannah Regional Minister Salisu Be-Awuribe has called for clear guidelines to distinguish between vote-buying and genuine acts of generosity, saying Ghana must establish what constitutes an electoral offence. Speaking to JoyNews in Damongo, the Regional Minister, who also chairs the Savannah Regional Security Council, said he had heard allegations of vote-buying but had personally not witnessed the practice. “I’ve heard it, but I’ve not witnessed it,” he said. Mr Be-Awuribe, however, acknowledged that Ghana’s electoral laws prohibit acts intended to influence voters. He referred to provisions under the Representation of the People’s Law, 1992 (PNDCL 284), which prohibit attempts to induce a person to vote, refrain from voting or influence another person’s electoral decision. “We’ve been doing politics. We do the best of what we think we can. But as to whether or not they are vote-buying is another aspect of it,” he said. The Minister was responding to concerns about the growing discussion around vote-buying in Ghanaian politics and whether financial or material support provided to voters could amount to electoral inducement. Mr Be-Awuribe said the difficulty was determining when an act of generosity or support becomes an attempt to influence a person’s electoral decision. He explained that politicians and community members often engage in exchanges that may not necessarily have an electoral motive. He cited an example from his experience as a Regional Minister. “I’ve visited a community, and the community possibly might be interested in getting development, and they want me to be a friend of that community,” he said. He explained that following such a visit, community members might offer gifts as a gesture of appreciation. “I come home, they are giving me some tubers of yam, a goat, and some other dishes, as a show of appreciation of the fact that the Regional Minister has come to their community,” he said. According to him, such a gesture, on its own, may not necessarily amount to an attempt to influence an electoral decision. “That in itself, they may be having some intent, which might not be explicit to me,” he explained. “But at any point in time that you make your intent expressed in that, there is a likelihood that, of course, you put yourself in those shoes,” he added. Need for clearer rules Mr Be-Awuribe said the behaviour of politicians and prospective candidates could also influence how communities interpret their actions. He noted that when someone who was previously not known for regularly visiting communities or providing assistance suddenly changes their behaviour, people may interpret the change as an indication that the person intends to contest an election. “Your behaviour, sometimes the community can read between the lines, that by this new act or behaviour that you have put up, you are likely to stand for some position,” he said. He said such a person could suddenly become more generous or more involved in the affairs of a community. “You have now introduced some sense of generosity, which you were not known for,” he said. “You were not visiting the communities, or you were not visiting them, but now you are regular. You are now interested in actually paying for their medical bills and others.” Asked whether paying the school fees of a constituent’s child, settling a person’s medical bill or providing other forms of assistance could amount to vote-buying when the beneficiary is a potential voter, Mr Be-Awuribe said Ghana needed clear and practical guidelines on the issue. “I think that as a country, we have the need for it there,” he said. He acknowledged that there were instances where people provided financial assistance while pursuing political ambitions, but stressed the need to clearly identify which actions should be considered prohibited. “We must come up with clear, defined guidelines as to what are or which elements are we considering as prohibitive acts,” he said. The Minister said the issue could not simply be determined by examining one isolated act. Instead, he said there should be clear standards to determine whether an action amounts to an attempt to influence an election, with a practical distinction between legitimate community support and conduct intended to induce voters. Mr Be-Awuribe also stressed that conduct prohibited by electoral law could have legal consequences. “It doesn’t matter that one thing in a way. If this didn’t happen, that is actually a criminal offence under the PNDCL 284,” he said. His comments come amid growing discussions about vote-buying and the use of money and other forms of assistance in Ghanaian politics. For the Savannah Regional Minister, the key issue is not simply whether politicians or individuals give money or other items to people, but whether such acts are intended to influence electoral choices.

items.title: Législatives en Russie : un scrutin tenu «dans un contexte d’escalade de menaces sans précédent»
items.description: « Cette campagne electorale, nous l'avons repete bien des fois, a ete tres differente de toutes les precedentes », a declare ce 25 septembre la presidente de la Commission electorale centrale (CEC), Ella Pamfilova, lors d'une reunion a la Douma consacree a la certification des resultats des legislatives. Elle a notamment oppose ce scrutin aux elections de 2021, qui s'etaient deroulees dans des « conditions de temps de paix ». « Elle s'en est distinguee avant tout par le fait qu'elle s'est tenue dans un contexte d'escalade de menaces sans precedent, sous toutes les formes », a-t-elle insiste, pointant du doigt la « pression colossale » exercee sur les membres des commissions electorales par les ennemis et evoquant « un flot constant de menaces » et de provocations durant ces legislatives. Six membres de commissions electorales, dont cinq femmes, ont ete tues durant la periode electorale. La responsable de la CEC a notamment cite Elena Astanina , presidente d'un bureau de vote dans la region de Zaporojie, tuee lors d'une attaque de drone ukrainien. La campagne « la plus complexe » de l'histoire de la Russie contemporaine « Nous n'avons pas pu eviter les pertes humaines causees par les monstres banderistes de Zelensky, ennemi non seulement du peuple russe, mais aussi de son propre peuple ukrainien qu'il extermine, ce meurtrier d'enfants », a fustige Pamfilova. « La combinaison de l'ampleur gigantesque de cette campagne, qui a ete veritablement massive, a plusieurs niveaux, et des conditions difficiles dans lequel elle s'est deroulee, sous le coup des sanctions et de pressions exterieures, permet d'affirmer que la Journee de vote unique 2026 a ete la campagne electorale la plus complexe sur le plan organisationnel de toute l'histoire de la Russie contemporaine », a-t-elle declare devant l'assemblee. Malgre ces ingerences exterieures, violentes, la campagne s'est deroulee avec « succes », avec un taux de participation de 59,80 %, 67 448 094 Russes s'etant deplaces aux urnes, a-t-elle precise. Les militaires du SVO parmi les electeurs les plus actifs et les plus engages En matiere de sieges, le parti presidentiel Russie Unie obtient 349 sieges, soit 25 de plus qu'en 2021, un record. En progression egalement, « Les gens nouveaux » avec 19 deputes contre 13 precedemment. Premier parti d'opposition, le Parti communiste (KPRF) en obtient 37, en net recul de 20 sieges. Meme tendance du cote de « Russie juste » qui, avec 17 deputes elus, perd 10 sieges. Le Parti liberal-democrate de Russie (LDPR) progresse de deux sieges, avec 23 deputes elus. Quant au parti « Patrie », il se maintient a seul un siege. Quatre sieges ont par ailleurs ete obtenus par des candidats sans etiquettes. « Je tiens a mettre tout particulierement en evidence le vote des electeurs militaires se trouvant dans la zone de l'operation militaire speciale. Ils se sont reveles etre les electeurs les plus actifs et les plus engages », a declare Pamfilova. Ces militaires comprennent « parfaitement pourquoi ils se battent et a quel point il est important que tout se passe bien a l'arriere, les elections constituant un element essentiel de cette normalite ». Par ailleurs, 46 veterans de l'operation militaire speciale (SVO) ont ete elus. Cela represente plus de 10 % du nombre total de sieges, a precise la cheffe de la CEC, ajoutant que parmi ces nouveaux deputes, 41 sont issus de Russie unie et trois du Parti liberal-democrate.

items.title: Burkina Faso : le retour des pluies relance les espoirs pour la campagne agropastorale 2026-2027
items.description: Les pluies sont revenues dans plusieurs regions du Burkina Faso apres plusieurs semaines de deficit hydrique qui avaient fait craindre une baisse des rendements agricoles. Du 21 au 23 septembre, des precipitations parfois abondantes ont contribue a rehumidifier les sols et a soutenir les cultures dans plusieurs communes agricoles. Le ministere burkinabe de l'Agriculture a indique que, dans les provinces du Ziro et de la Sissili, les cumuls avaient atteint 68,2 mm a Cassou, 52 mm a Gao, 46 mm a Boura et 38 mm a Leo dans la nuit du 21 au 22 septembre. D'autres regions du pays ont egalement enregistre des precipitations importantes, avec des cumuls allant notamment de 38 mm dans le Goulmou a 56 mm dans le Djoro, a Gueguere et a Iolonioro. Selon les previsions de l'Agence nationale de la meteorologie du Burkina Faso, la periode du 21 au 27 septembre devrait rester « tres humide », avec des cumuls pouvant atteindre 50 mm, voire davantage, dans plusieurs localites. Ces pluies ravivent l'espoir de sauver pres de 20 000 hectares de cultures, avait indique le ministre de l'Agriculture, Ismael Sombie, lors d'une tournee de suivi de la campagne agricole effectuee a la mi-septembre. Le ministre a toutefois souligne que, malgre le deficit pluviometrique observe ces dernieres semaines, les progres enregistres en 2026 dans l'extension des superficies emblavees n'etaient pas remis en cause. Le gouvernement burkinabe a par ailleurs assure qu'il poursuivait le suivi de l'etat des cultures afin d'evaluer l'impact des recentes precipitations sur la campagne agricole. Les autorites burkinabe avaient fait etat, en août dernier, de resultats juges historiques dans le cadre de l'offensive agropastorale et halieutique 2023-2025, portant sur plusieurs filieres vivrieres ainsi que sur les productions animale et halieutique. Fort de ces resultats, le gouvernement a lance, le 30 juillet, une nouvelle initiative baptisee « Offensive agropastorale, hydraulique et halieutique 2026-2028 », avec pour objectif de renforcer l'autosuffisance alimentaire du pays.

items.title: TOR secures 950,000 barrels of Sankofa crude from GNPC
items.description: The Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) has received 950,000 barrels of crude oil from Ghana’s Sankofa-Gye Nyame field through a partnership with the Ghana National Petroleum Corporation (GNPC), marking the refinery’s first time processing crude from the field. Supplied through GNPC and transported by Sonangol Cazenga, the crude will be refined at TOR into petroleum products for the Ghanaian market. The development is expected to boost Ghana’s domestic refining capacity and support greater use of locally produced crude to meet domestic fuel needs. Sankofa crude is shipped in cargoes of approximately 950,000 barrels. TOR said the shipment highlights the potential for stronger collaboration between Ghana’s upstream and downstream petroleum sectors, with locally produced crude being directed towards domestic refining. The Managing Director of TOR said the partnership with GNPC provides an opportunity to strengthen the refinery’s operations while retaining more value from Ghana’s petroleum resources within the country. The delivery of Sankofa crude marks an important milestone for TOR, according to its managing director, who believes the development will contribute to a stronger, more resilient and sustainable petroleum industry. The shipment comes as TOR continues efforts to restore full operations following extensive turnaround maintenance. In his 2026 State of the Nation Address, President John Dramani Mahama noted that the refinery had resumed crude processing for the first time since 2018. The refinery said the collaboration also supports the government’s efforts to strengthen integration across the upstream, midstream, and downstream segments of the petroleum industry. The refinery indicated that TOR and GNPC are expected to identify and pursue additional areas of collaboration. The Managing Director of TOR also commended President Mahama and Energy Minister John Abdulai Jinapor for their support. He extended his appreciation to GNPC’s management, as well as the refinery’s tolling partners, Fujairah and Triangle Commodities Trading, for their ongoing cooperation and support.

items.title: FIFA : les ligues anglaise, espagnole, italienne et allemande réclament une réforme de la gouvernance
items.description: Les quatre principales ligues européennes (la Premier League anglaise, la Liga espaqnole, la Serie A italienne et la Bundesliga allemande) ont appelé vendredi à une réforme de la gouvernance de la Fifa, plongée dans la crise depuis la révélation du projet avorté de création d'une société commerciale ouverte à des investisseurs privés. « Une réforme fondamentale de la gouvernance est indispensable pour rétablir des limites statutaires claires au sein de la Fifa et garantir, de manière démontrable, que les dossiers disciplinaires individuels restent à l'abri de toute ingérence politique », ont écrit les quatre ligues dans un communiqué transmis à l'AFP. Cette demande intervient alors que le président de la Fifa, Gianni Infantino, fragilisé après avoir mené sans concertation le projet de création d'une société commerciale, baptisée Fifa Forward Entreprise (FFE), et candidat à sa propre succession en mars 2027, a proposé lundi « une consultation » des fédérations afin de réformer la gouvernance de l'instance. « Le président de la Fifa a certes reconnu la nécessité d'une réforme, mais il ne suffit pas d'envisager des changements superficiels ou procéduraux au lendemain de l'affaire FFE », indiquant ainsi les quatre principales ligues européennes qui qualifient le projet FFE de « l'un des plus graves abus de pouvoir de l'histoire de l'instance ». la Premier League, la Liga, la Serie A et la Bundesliga proposent ainsi la mise en place d' « une instance permanente » représentant « les associations nationales, les ligues, les clubs et les joueurs, tant du football masculin que féminin ». items.title: NAGRAT calls for probe into alleged inflation of School Feeding enrolment figures
items.description: The President of the National Association of Graduate Teachers (NAGRAT), Jacob Anaba, has called for an immediate audit of school enrolment figures used to determine allocations under the National School Feeding Programme. His call follows concerns raised by the National Coordinator of the School Feeding Programme, Hajia Fati Forgor, that some head teachers allegedly inflate pupil enrolment figures to secure higher allocations, potentially depriving genuinely needy schools of adequate support. Mr Anaba said the allegations must be thoroughly investigated to establish the extent of the practice and identify those responsible. He described the alleged manipulation of enrolment figures as a serious abuse of responsibility that cheats the state and undermines the objectives of the programme. “If you have been given a position to deliver something to our kids, a critical one at that, and you are inflating the figures, it means that you are cheating the system, the state, and we shouldn’t allow that to pass.” Mr Anaba said an audit would help verify the actual number of pupils in beneficiary schools and ensure that allocations were based on accurate data. “We will call for an audit to show that we can find out those who are doing that and bring them to book,” he said in an interview with Citi FM. According to the NAGRAT President, accurate enrolment data is essential to ensuring that resources under the School Feeding Programme are distributed fairly and reach the pupils who need them. He also called for greater attention to the nutritional quality of meals served to pupils under the programme. Mr Anaba said meals provided at schools should contain sufficient nutrients to support the health, concentration and learning of children. “The food they give to our children in the school should be something that will nourish them, will give them the nourishment that they can be able to sustain in the classroom.” He stressed that the School Feeding Programme plays an important role in supporting pupils’ participation in school and should therefore be implemented transparently and effectively.

items.title: What Annie Dillard Left Out
items.description: This is an edition of the Books Briefing, our editors’ weekly guide to the best in books. Sign up for it here. Annie Dillard, who recently died at 81, understood that even in suburban landscapes, one could experience the transcendence and solitude of nature. Reading Diana Saverin’s Atlantic essay about Dillard’s great nature writing made me remember the joy of exploring the wetlands behind my elementary school on the outskirts of Denver, where cottony cattails burst open, crayfish scuttled in the creek, and I could spend hours gazing into a bush, attempting to catch sight of the fairies I was sure lived inside. First, here are four new stories from The Atlantic ’s Books section: The confrontation that broke New York Six hard-to-find books worth reading The book claiming to teach couples how to select their baby’s sex “Pinballing,” a poem by Jan Beatty In her classic book Pilgrim at Tinker Creek , for example, Dillard describes being “knocked breathless by a powerful glance” in an ordinary Virginia backyard: Gazing at a cedar tree outside a home in her neighborhood, she suddenly experienced it as “charged and transfigured.” But her work suggests that to be deeply in nature is to be in some way separated from other humans. Perhaps this is one reason, as Saverin writes, that Dillard’s personal relationships are largely absent from her writing. That’s true in my memories of the wetlands, too: I must have been able to hear passing sirens, or see airplanes overhead, but my memories involve no such intrusions. In fact, I barely remember my fellow students. I know they were there; I remember cajoling one to examine my beloved shrub turned fairy palace. But the images feel solitary. Dillard captured exactly this sense of observational aloneness. I suspect such selective attention occurs for the same reason that, while looking at a work of art closely, you may cease to notice the museumgoers around you. To view something intensely is to blur your own boundaries, such that you become as much the thing you watch as the person you are. I understand why, for Dillard and some of her fellow nature writers, other people can be difficult to bring into the frame. They’re an interruption: As soon as someone says your name, you’re no longer immersed. But Saverin, who deeply loves Dillard’s work, still wonders what else she might have achieved by bringing a bit more of human presence into her considerations of the natural world. “Part of the pain of losing someone, and perhaps especially a favorite writer,” she writes, “involves losing what they didn’t choose to make during the time they had.” Jill Krementz The Enduring Mystery of Annie Dillard By Diana Saverin Dillard kept much of her personal life carefully outside the scope of her nonfiction. Read the full article. What to Read Yesterday’s Burdens , by Robert M. Coates If Coates survives in historical memory, it’s as a Lost Generation footnote—the man who first introduced Ernest Hemingway to Gertrude Stein. This is an unfortunate legacy, though, for an audacious American literary experimenter whose 1926 debut, The Eater of Darkness , was called “the first Dada novel in English.” Because Coates worked for three decades as The New Yorker ’s art critic, something of a painter’s visual language is found in his strange, oblique sentences. My favorite of his novels is Yesterday’s Burdens , of which Stein was an admirer. (“It is so exciting because it is modern,” she declared.) The novel follows the restless Henderson, a young man who wanders Manhattan, visiting speakeasies and crashing parties to keep despair at bay. Coates absorbs the city’s fabulous energies and arranges the tumult into rich, cubist sketches that reproduce overlapping advertising slogans, subway signs, motor cars, and overheard conversations. After being out of print for decades, Yesterday’s Burdens was resurrected in 2020 by Tough Poets Press. Rife with formal oddities and stylistic verve, this masterpiece captures New York in language that still feels fresh nearly a century later. — Dustin Illingworth From our list: Six hard-to-find books worth reading Out Next Week 📚 The Floating World , by Ben Eastham 📚 Bad Boy for Life: The Rise and Fall of Sean Combs , by Cheyenne Roundtree 📚 To Jerusalem and Back: A Personal Account , by Saul Bellow Your Weekend Read Illustration by Matteo Giuseppe Pani / The Atlantic. Source: Getty. America’s Hypocritical Take on Intellectual Property By Alex Reisner Encyclopedia Britannica , the publisher of Chicken Soup for the Soul , and Strike 3, an adult-film company, may not seem to have much in common. But they all agree on one thing: They want payment for the use of their work in training AI models. In the past year, each of them has brought a lawsuit against the big AI companies, claiming that their content was used to train models without permission. Read the full article. items.title: Poutine : la Russie était prête à reprendre les négociations après les législatives, mais Kiev a ciblé Moscou
items.description: « Ils doivent ressentir les ripostes de l'armee russe et comprendre que toutes leurs provocations, leurs tentatives d'aggraver la situation sont absolument inutiles, qu'elles ne deboucheront sur aucun resultat concret et ne feront qu'aggraver leur situation. » Depuis Saint-Petersbourg, ou se tenait ce 25 septembre le XIIe Forum international des cultures unies, Vladimir Poutine a renvoye les dirigeants kieviens a leurs responsabilites dans l'absence de pourparlers de paix. « En effet, nous avons dit qu'il etait peu probable que des negociations soient possibles avant les elections a la Douma et que nous serions prets a reprendre ces contacts par la suite », a declare le chef d'etat russe, apres une allusion aux declarations de Volodymyr Zelensky, selon lesquelles une reprise de pourparlers directs avec la Russie etait envisageable des le mois de septembre, apres les legislatives du 18-20. « Qu'est-ce qui s'est passe depuis ? », a interpelle le president russe, avant de rappeler que dans « la nuit du 19 au 20 septembre, le jour principal du vote, une tentative a ete faite pour effectuer une frappe massive contre Moscou. Premierement, plus de 1 600 drones sont pratiquement entres dans la zone de Moscou ». Attaques ukrainiennes : la Russie a « commence a repliquer sur chaque point » Vladimir Poutine est egalement revenu sur les attaques visant des bureaux de vote et des membres de commissions electorales. Plus tot dans la journee, devant la Douma, la presidente de la Commission electorale centrale, Ella Pamfilova, avait cite les noms de six membres de commissions electorales qui ont ete tues par des attaques ukrainiennes dans le cadre de ces elections legislatives. Le president russe a egalement rappele les nombreuses attaques contre les navires « aussi bien russes que battant pavillon etranger » en mer Noire, ainsi que la campagne « 40 jours » de frappes, dont s'etait enorgueilli Volodymyr Zelensky sur les reseaux sociaux fin juin. « Toutes ces actions ne font qu'empirer leur situation », a fustige le chef d'etat russe. « Les pistes d'une eventuelle reconciliation et les propositions de reprise des negociations sont bien sur la table et restent realisables », a-t-il poursuivi, « mais apres tout ce qu'ils ont fait, nous allons bien reflechir a ce que nous devrions entreprendre en reponse ». Vladimir Poutine a assure que les forces russes avaient « commence a repliquer sur chaque point ». « De toute evidence, les ripostes de l'armee russe se sont averees tellement douloureuses et devastatrices pour l'ennemi que celui-ci remet activement sur la table la question d'une treve sur plusieurs plans : le volet energetique, c'est-a-dire qu'ils sont desormais prets a ne plus frapper nos raffineries, et le volet aerien, en proposant un arret mutuel des frappes », a-t-il souligne, en reference aux declarations de Volodymyr Zelensky quant a un « moratoire energetique » et les appels du president francais Emmanuel Macron a un « double moratoire », tant sur l'energie qu'en mer Noire. Quant a ceux qui, en Europe, brandissent le spectre d'une attaque russe, « nous n'avons aucun plan de ce genre et surtout aucune raison, aucun motif d'aggraver la situation avec l'Europe », a reaffirme le president russe.

items.title: Four more arrested over alleged 2026 school placement fraud
items.description: Four more people, including a physician assistant in Kumasi, have been arrested over their alleged involvement in the 2026 school placement fraud. The arrests were made in Kumasi and at the Accra Resolution Centres as investigations into alleged attempts to manipulate the Computerised School Selection and Placement System (CSSPS) continue. In Kumasi, a physician assistant at the SDA Hospital, Yaw Adjei Boateng, was arrested on Thursday, September 24, and interrogated by officers of the Intelligence Unit. According to information available to the Ministry of Education from the Ghana Police Service, Yaw Adjei Boateng admitted knowing Vicentia Antwi Appiah and told investigators that she had contacted him to help secure placement for Benedicta Yaa Edinam at Mafe Methodist Girls’ Senior High School. He reportedly told investigators that he received GH¢8,500 from Vicentia Antwi Appiah and subsequently forwarded the money to his former schoolmate, Brian Opare Addo, who works at the Ashanti Regional Coordinating Council, to help facilitate the placement. The placement was unsuccessful, he reportedly told investigators. Yaw Adjei Boateng further claimed that he later instructed Brian Opare Addo to refund the money to Vicentia Antwi Appiah and that the refund was made. He also told investigators that Brian Opare Addo had previously helped him secure placement for another person at St Monica’s Senior High School. As part of the ongoing investigation, Brian Opare Addo has been invited to report to the Intelligence Unit on Monday, September 28, to assist with investigations. Meanwhile, two other persons were arrested at the Accra Resolution Centre on Friday, September 25, as the probe into the alleged school placement fraud widened. The latest arrests bring to four the number of persons arrested in connection with the investigation over the past 48 hours, with one other person invited to assist with the probe. The Police Service had previously arrested two individuals on September 17, 2026, over their alleged involvement in school placement fraud.

items.title: What Do We Do About the Cameras Everywhere?
items.description: Subscribe here: Apple Podcasts | Spotify | YouTube Meta has been selling millions of its camera-equipped glasses, making all of us fodder for content creation—when we’re on the street, at the store, and in our workplaces. Host Charlie Warzel talks with the Verge reporter Mia Sato about how regular people are being affected as these glasses increase in use, the backlash to Flock cameras, and what happens when we’re always being recorded. The following is a transcript of the episode: Mia Sato: I think Meta is kind of like perpetually getting in its own way. You know, it just can’t seem to figure out how to have people soften up to the company. And that’s why you see this rollout just being like a complete disaster, really. Charlie Warzel: Hey there, quick question. Is it a bad thing if people start referring to your AI-powered face computer as “pervert glasses”? I’m Charlie Warzel, and this is Galaxy Brain , a show where today we’re talking about Meta smart glasses and the slow and steady erosion of our public expectation of privacy, and whether or not Americans are actually mounting a genuine backlash to the surveillance state. Big tech companies have been trying to crack spatial and face computing for a long time. Arguably the most notable example was Google Glass, a Star Trek –looking headset that was, technologically speaking, pretty impressive, but cost about 1,500 bucks and mostly just repulsed people. The prototype program for Google Glass fizzled out, but not before I tried a pair 13 years ago, visiting Google’s headquarters one day. Google Glass may have failed, but it did produce the most cursed photograph that exists of me. Plenty have tried to make smart glasses a thing. Snapchat released its first version of its spectacles in 2016, but the product just didn’t really catch on. And that’s in part because the technology wasn’t quite there, or it was wonky or cumbersome, or there wasn’t enough memory or storage. And then, in 2021, Meta released its smart glasses. Its first collaboration was with the sunglasses company Ray-Ban. And Meta’s proposition here was that the glasses looked a lot more like actual glasses. Initially, the camera could record about 30 to 60 seconds of video, and the glasses let people listen to music or take calls, and the videos that were captured could be shared across Meta’s platforms, like Instagram and Facebook, using a special stories app. And from the launch, two things happened. First, the glasses caused a somewhat expected controversy around privacy, like all these devices tend to do. But second, the glasses were successful. People bought them. And for creators, especially, the product was something between a gimmick and a genuinely new, useful camera tool. And so Meta decided to invest in them. In 2023, they infused the glasses with AI software that allowed the glasses to describe what a user was looking at in their field of vision. Very fancy. And all the while, Meta has tried to dodge controversy, around whether the glasses will eventually deploy facial-recognition technology and over what data the company retains or uses to train its large language models. And for a while, the glasses were mostly just this. It was a curio used by creators and mostly despised by privacy advocates. But all that has really changed over the past year. In 2026, the glasses had become more popular and more prevalent, and there have been more examples of people abusing them. People filming women on the street for pickup-artist videos. Strange black markets popping up to hack cameras so that the recording light doesn’t show. And as more people wear the glasses, more people are concerned that they’re being surreptitiously recorded at sporting events, at dinner parties, at the store; maybe even being recorded while having sex. And this negative reaction, which started on social media, has spread thoroughly throughout popular culture. This summer, the late-night host Jimmy Kimmel referred to Meta’s device as “pervert glasses.” And yet the glasses keep selling. Celebrities are attaching their names and likenesses to them, and the abuses continue to pile up. And so it all seems like we are headed toward a genuine reckoning for both Meta, but all of us really. What is really going on here? Are these glasses here to stay? Are they impacting the lives of regular people? People who are just trying to go about their days and do their jobs? What happens to all of us in a world where we’re always being recorded? And crucially, what can you do if someone comes up to you on the street wearing a pair of these glasses? Mia Sato is a reporter and features writer at The Verge who has reported extensively on the ways that these glasses are upending people’s lives. What I like about her work is that it’s always situated on the ways that emerging technologies affect regular people. And so she joins me now to talk about all of this. Mia, welcome to Galaxy Brain . Sato: Thank you for having me. Warzel: So before we get into the current state of the Meta Glasses, the cameras everywhere, the panopticon world that we live in, I wanted to walk just a little bit through the history of these glasses with you. Kind of get your reaction to some of it. And this all starts on my birthday, September 9th, 2021. Facebook launches the glasses. Did you expect them to take off? I mean, this is—I’ll just put myself out there. I, at every moment with a facial wearable technology, like a camera-on-your-face kind of situation, I always expect it to fail. I mean, everyone was very excited about Apple’s Vision Pro a couple of years ago, and I was just like, I don’t think we’re ready for it yet. But like—did you expect this to be an actual product category for Meta that was gonna work, or did you sort of feel like it was destined for the same dustbin? Sato: I think at the time, and what I still believe, is that this will not be adopted in the way that Meta says it will or hopes it will. And to me, the most straightforward reason is that not everyone wants to wear glasses. Like, sometimes people don’t want something on their face. And this was kind of the thing that I couldn’t get over with the Vision Pro and other headsets and stuff is like—that’s a really big barrier to entry. Having something on your head, having something on your face that covers, you know, your hair, your makeup; like, there are all sorts of weird human things that that is just like a barrier, literally. Warzel: So I’ve picked out a couple of events here that I think are related in the history of these glasses. And the first is in 2024, Meta confirmed to TechCrunch that images and videos shared with Meta AI—for an example, the look and ask features—may be used to improve Meta’s AI models. So these glasses, you know, the input outputs are going to be used to train artificial-intelligence systems. The second is in April 2025, in an email to glasses owners, Meta said that AI features, including Meta with a camera, would be on by default—and that voice recordings would be stored by default, with no opt-out. This year, confusingly, Meta tells The Guardian that, “unless users choose to share media that they’ve captured with Meta or others, that media stays on the user’s device. And when people share content with Meta AI, we sometimes use contractors to review this data for the purpose of improving people’s experience. We take steps to filter the data and protect people’s privacy.” These feel like important revelations to me, because so much of the concern about these glasses is that they’ll be used to surveil others. But isn’t it just as important of a story how much these glasses are surveilling their owners? Sato: Totally. You are giving up an incredible amount of information about yourself and what you do every day simply by maybe wearing these glasses. And I think, you know, there’s obviously the fears around how other people—who are sort of unwitting participants in your glasses journey—how their information is being captured and stored and used later. But it’s kind of incredible to me that with this sort of back-and-forth flip-flopping, more glasses users aren’t asking, like: I just wore them all day. What do you know about my life? That’s a huge reason why I personally wouldn’t use these glasses. Because I am like—there are some things that I actually would prefer Meta not know about me. They know a lot already. But there’s some stuff that I would like to keep for myself. Warzel: Right. And so, okay, this brings us to earlier this year, February 2026. And The New York Times publishes a report that I think cast the company in as poor a light as I’ve ever seen an internal memo cast on a tech company. The story alleges that Meta is talking internally about adding facial recognition back into its glasses. And the Times gets a hold of a document from May of the previous year, which described these plans to release Name Tag, which is its codename for a facial-recognition product. They plan to release it to attendees of a conference for the blind, which the company didn’t actually do. But this was part of what they were gonna do. And there’s a line from the internal memo that made news, which is: “We will launch during a dynamic political environment, where many civil-society groups that we would expect to attack us would have their resources focused on other concerns.” That’s according to a document from Meta’s Reality Labs, which works on hardware including smart glasses. I just want, first, to get your reaction to that. Like what are people supposed to make of that? That this company that is making this stuff is hoping that people will be busy enough attending to the other horrors of the world so as not to focus on the actual product that they’re rolling out. Like—tell me what to make of that. Sato: I mean, we have so many gadgets and tech that is beyond what people could have imagined we had, right? We have computers in our phones, and that is amazing. And I think we kind of skip over the fact that the idea of glasses that can record people around you and maybe even recognize who they are is literally like the spyglasses of the kids’ movies that I watched growing up, right? Like, that’s like Spy Kids —would love to have glasses that can record your whole day, and you can ask them later what you saw. As Meta, some leaked plans have suggested Meta’s working on, or recognize the people around you. So the capability is so sci-fi, futuristic spyware that I just want to make sure we take a moment to be like: This is really crazy technology that we’re talking about. And the point about accessibility—the role of glasses in disability spaces, this is something that Meta has harped on quite a bit. And it’s true, and my colleagues at The Verge have done great work about how these tools can be used for accessibility purposes. But there’s a pattern of Meta kind of putting them into these spaces and almost trying to deflect from the larger privacy and surveillance concerns that people have, including people who are disabled. Like, disabled people also deserve privacy. So there’s a real push and pull between, like, “What can these glasses be used for?” and “What settings could we use, could we put them in?” Versus, like, “What is the worst version of how someone could use this technology?” Which is always going to be the thing that the public thinks about. Like—what danger does this pose to me, to my kids, to my life day to day? And you know, right now, a lot of the news stories that we’re reading, and the story that I wrote, was about some of the people who are doing the worst version of that. So it’s sort of like a shadow cast over Meta and this new line item that they hope will become a major part of how people interact with their company. Warzel : And this, to me, this idea of “We wanna launch during a period of time when people—but especially like, you know, civil-liberties groups—aren’t gonna be paying as much attention about this.” To say nothing of taking advantage of horrific world events or political events? It suggests that they know this is creeping people out, to some degree. That, to me, feels like they have lost in that sense the cover of saying, No, no, no—we think this is just going to be a great thing for the world. Like—everyone should want these, and they’re gonna empower people to do great things. Sato: It’s also, you know, a reality that Meta is feeling the heat for these glasses. Like they are synonymous and some people have called them “pervert glasses” or “glasses for creeps,” right? Like, the rollout is so messy. It’s such—it’s really just not a good look. And I think Meta, just even zooming out from the hardware stuff, Meta has lost a lot of public trust over the last decade, and over the last like five years. And it’s facing all of these battles. Not just that people think the glasses are creepy, but that it’s facing all these court cases. And it’s being sued by parents and states for, you know, its products and how it harms young people— Warzel: And losing— Sato : —and losing. And I thought your advice was reasonably sound. So I wanted to ask you, just as we wrap up here, some of your thoughts—like, guideline-etiquette rules for using these glasses or encountering these glasses in the wild. And so I guess, first up, even if you disagree with the fact that someone has purchased these in general, what’s your etiquette advice for people when it comes to using them around other people, out in the world? Sato: Well, I think, if you’re with your friends, it depends on the setting, I guess. But I would say maybe let people know. Just say, you know: I’m wearing these glasses; I’m not recording; I’m not doing anything with them. You know what I mean? Warzel: Sounds like a super-cool thing to do at a party. Hey guys, I’m wearing these glasses. Sato: I know. Informed consent when you hang out with your friends. But that’s another part of this—like, these glasses really are a hindrance. Because who wants to say: Just so you know, I’m wearing these glasses that a lot of you really hate. But, like, I’m not doing the thing that you really hate. So don’t worry. But you know, I would probably say you should let people know. Because I think a lot of the bristling comes from the fact that people are realizing after the fact. Like: Wait a minute; are those Meta Glasses? And then it becomes a problem. Obviously, like don’t cover the light. That’s really creepy. That’s really weird and strange, strange thing to do. And I get that, you know, it’s useful for other things; like, some people really like listening to music that way. I get it. But you have to be sort of prepared for people to push back on it. Which I think is like—you know, that’s something that you don’t have to do if you have normal glasses. Warzel: This wonderfully brings us to the last question, which is: If you see them out in the wild, and you feel like somebody might be up in your space, possibly filming you or just making you a little uncomfortable, what is your advice—having talked to a lot of these people and reporting on these situations? What’s your advice for somebody who finds themselves in that situation? Sato: Yeah, I will say my understanding is that if you get close enough and say, Hey Meta, stop recording , it could work. There, the users can disable the voice-activation setting where it’s like, that doesn’t work. But it responds to any voice, not just the wearer’s voice. So if you think someone is recording—like, you see the light on the glasses on—you could try getting right up to them. And say, Hey Meta, stop recording , to see if that works. It might not always, but may be worth a shot if you really are feeling harassed. Warzel: Hey Meta, delete my account. Just unplug the servers. Sato : Hey Meta, forget I exist . Warzel: Jeez. Mia, thank you so much for coming on Galaxy Brain to talk about this. And thank you for your reporting, which I think has really shown the human impact of all this technology in the world. Thank you for all your work. Sato: Yeah; my pleasure. Warzel: If you liked what you saw here, new episodes of Galaxy Brain drop every Friday. You can subscribe on The Atlantic ’s YouTube channel, or on Apple or Spotify, or wherever it is that you get your podcasts. And if you want to support this work, and the work of my fellow colleagues, you can subscribe to the publication at TheAtlantic.com/Listener. That’s TheAtlantic.com/Listener. Thanks so much, and I’ll see you on the internet. This episode of Galaxy Brain was produced by Hadley Robinson; the video was edited by Denny Thomas; and the audio was engineered by Miguel Carrascal. Our theme is by Rob Smierciak. Claudine Ebeid is the executive producer of Atlantic audio, and Andrea Valdez is our managing editor. Learn more about your ad choices. items.title: Commune de Bignona : une quarantaine d’arbres dangereux abattus
items.description: 42 arbres à risques sont abattus et ont servi à fabriquer 550 tables-bancs dédiés aux établissements scolaires de la commune. BIGNONA – Au total, 37 arbres sont abattus et 5 autres élagués, soit au total 42 arbres dans la commune de Bignona. Il s’agissait d’arbres centenaires qui menaçaient la quiétude des populations. Ces arbres sont transformés en tables-bancs réfectionnés gratuitement par les acteurs de la chaîne de valeur, notamment les exploitants forestiers, les menuisiers, les soudeurs qui ont accompagné le processus par leurs propres moyens au bénéfice de 11 écoles élémentaires et 3 collèges de la commune. Même les commerçants ont participé à travers l’achat de la peinture. « Dans ce contexte de rentrée scolaire, ce dont vient répondre à notre déficit en tables-bancs estimé à 690 tables-bancs », a magnifié Boubacar Konaté, Inspecteur de l’éducation et de la formation (IEF) de Bignona 2 vendredi à la réunion de restitution des travaux des opérations d’abattage et d’élagage d’arbres menaçant chute dans la commune de Bignona. Les communes de Djibidione et Oulampane, zones de retour des déplacés du conflit en Casamance, ont aussi bénéficié à raison de 20 tables-bancs chacune. Au total, 550 tables-bancs sont confectionnées et seront livrées dans les 10 prochains jours. Un déficit de tables-bancs noté dans la commune « Dès demain, les opérations de montage vont démarrer dans les 14 établissements qui ont bénéficié de ces tables-bancs », a indiqué Boubacar Konaté. Avec ce don, le déficit est réduit à 140 tables-bancs pour la commune. De leur côté, les soudeurs se sont engagés à aller monter les tables-bancs partout où elles seront destinées, y compris au niveau des lointaines communes de Djibidione et Oulampane. La mairie de Bignona, qui est à l'origine de l'initiative d’abattage des arbres, s'est engagée à reboiser les axes et lieux concernés par l’opération d’abattage et d’élagage des vieux cailcédrats. « Nous allons mettre des caïlcédrats par endroits mais aussi nous allons choisir d’autres espèces avec l’encadrement des eaux et forêts », a déclaré le maire de Bignona, Bacary Diatta. A lire aussi : Bignona : un élan communautaire pour restaurer 10 hectares de mangrove Mamadou Khouma, préfet du département de Bignona, a salué l’engagement citoyen et communautaire des exploitants forestiers, des menuisiers, des soudeurs qui ont aussi décidé de réparer gratuitement toutes les carcasses de tables-bancs. « Il y a un engagement communautaire. Même pour la distribution de ces tables-bancs, il y a une solidarité départementale parce que les arbres sont abattus dans la commune de Bignona, mais on va donner une part à Djibidione et Oulampane pour accompagner ces deux communes où il y a des villages de retour, de nouvelles créations », a dit magnifié le préfet. Kadidiatou SONKO (Correspondante)

items.title: 646 military recruits pass out after six-month infantry training at Shai Hills
items.description: A total of 646 recruits have successfully completed the Basic Infantry Training Course 1-26 (BITC 1-26) of the Ghana Armed Forces (GAF) at a colourful pass-out parade held at the Army Recruit Training School (ARTS), Shai Hills in the Shai-Osudoku District. According to GAF, the ceremony, held on Friday, September 25, marked the completion of six months of intensive military training for the recruits. The Reviewing Officer, General Officer Commanding (GOC), Southern Command, Brigadier General Edward Awaribey, commended the recruits for their resilience and commitment throughout the training period. He reminded them that the pass-out parade marked only the beginning of their military careers, stressing the importance of continuous learning, humility and strict discipline in building successful careers in the Ghana Armed Forces. Brigadier General Awaribey also cautioned the newly trained soldiers against using military uniforms for unauthorised activities, including land guarding, debt collection and involvement in personal disputes. He urged them to exercise caution on social media to avoid compromising operational security and advised them to stay away from illicit substances. The Reviewing Officer further charged the recruits to uphold the core values of discipline, integrity, courage and loyalty to the Constitution as they begin their service in the Ghana Armed Forces. Outstanding recruits honoured The pass-out ceremony also featured awards for recruits and companies that distinguished themselves in various military disciplines during the six-month training programme. Recruit Ebenezer Akwasi Midorse emerged as the overall standout performer, receiving both the Chief of the Army Staff’s Award for Overall Best Recruit and the award for Best in Tactics. Recruit Sarah Nyarkowaa Twum was adjudged the Overall Best Female Recruit and received the Chief Staff Officer’s Army Headquarters Award. Other individual awards went to Recruit Stephen Atendana Solomba, who was recognised as Best in Drill, while Recruit Alfred Asare Koranteng received the Commander, Army Training Command’s Award for Academic Excellence. At the company level, Kamina Company was adjudged the Overall Best Company after emerging victorious in both the cross-country and steeplechase competitions.

Pakistan secure another Asian Games medal as Noor, Ashab reach squash semis
items.description: Pakistan secured another medal at the Asian Games on Friday after Noor Zaman and Mohammad Ashab Irfan won their respective singles matches to reach the semi-finals of the squash competition. Third-seeded Noor defeated Hong Kong’s Chi Hin Henry Leung, while fifth-seeded Ashab overcame India’s Veer Chotrani at the Nagoya Kinjo Futo Arena to put Pakistan into the medal rounds of the event. Noor, Pakistan’s top-ranked player in the draw, was pushed by Leung but held his nerve to secure a place in the last four. Ashab also produced a strong performance against the fourth-seeded Indian, recovering from losing the opening game to win 3-1. Ashab prevailed 6-11, 11-8, 11-6, 11-6 to avenge Pakistan’s defeat to India in the men’s team final at the previous Asian Games. The victories mean Pakistan are assured of at least a bronze medal in the men’s singles competition, with the losing semi-finalists awarded bronze. It is the first time since 2002 that two players for Pakistan have made it to the Asian Games semi-finals The two Pakistanis had reached the quarter-finals without dropping a game, with Noor defeating Kuwait’s Ammar Altamimi 11-4, 11-9, 11-4 and Ashab overcoming Saudi Arabia’s Mohammad Al Alnafsan 11-9, 11-3, 11-5 in the last 16 on Thursday. Noor and Ashab will now contest their respective semi-finals on Saturday, with a place in Sunday’s final at stake. Meanwhile, Pakistan’s mixed doubles pair of Asim Khan and Mehwish Ali saw their run halted at the quarter-final stage — the lone blemish on an otherwise promising day for the country’s racquet sport. Asim and Mehwish, who had battled back from a game down to reach the last eight, could not summon another comeback, going down to Hong Kong’s Cheuk Nam Lai and Yee Lam Toby Tse 6-11, 7-11 in 20 minutes. In fencing, Pakistan’s men’s foil team crashed out at the table of 16 stage, losing 45-12 to China at the Aichi Sky Expo. The trio of Mohammad Waqas, Abdul Musawir and Baryal Khan managed just eight bout wins across nine relays, with China controlling the tie from start to finish. Pakistan also received one yellow card and one red card during the match, further denting their hopes against the hosts. The defeat ends Pakistan’s run in the men’s foil team competition. At the Tokyo Aquatics Centre, Mishael Aisha Hayat Ayub finished second last in the women’s 50m butterfly heat with a time of 30.95 seconds. Overall, the 24-year-old finished 25th among 27 competitors, with Chinese Taipei’s An-chi Han the last to qualify in 27.13. Hamza Asif also failed to advance from his heat, finishing fifth in the men’s 50m breaststroke in 30.47 seconds. His time placed him 35th among 40 swimmers, with Kazakhstan’s Aibat Myrzamuratov taking the last qualifying spot in 27.86. The badminton campaign got off to a disastrous start as Pakistan lost both of their fixtures in the men’s singles and mixed doubles at the Ichinomiya City Municipal Gymnasium. Mohammad Ali Larosh lost his first-round singles fixture against Kazakhstan’s Makhsut Tajibullayev 2-1. Larosh made a slow start, losing nine points on his own service to drop the first game 11-21. The 30-year-old then came back strongly in the second, breaking his opponent 14 times to wrap up the game 24-22 on the third game point and force a decider. The decider proved an end-to-end thriller, with Larosh at one point five points up, but the Kazakh held his nerve to overcome the deficit and knock out Larosh 22-24 as he failed to save the second match point. Larosh could not make amends in the mixed doubles, as he and Mahoor Shahzad bowed out after being brushed aside by South Korea’s Yun Jaeh Kim and Hajeong Jang 1-21, 10-21. In athletics, Pakistan’s Noreen Hussain failed to register a mark in the women’s pole vault final.

items.title: Ouagadougou: un réseau clandestin de fabrication et de reconditionnement de boissons alcoolisées démasqué
items.description: La police municipale de Ouagadougou a démasqué un réseau clandestin de fabrication et de reconditionnement de boissons alcoolisées et interpellé des individus pour la suite de l’investigation, selon une information de la structure, ce vendredi 25 septembre 2026. Le mardi 22 septembre 2026, suite à une dénonciation, la Direction de la Sécurité Publique (DSP) a mené une intervention dans l’arrondissement n°06 de la Commune de Ouagadougou, visant un réseau présumé impliqué dans des activités clandestines de fabrication et de reconditionnement de boissons alcoolisées au sein d’une cour. Selon le texte de la Police municipale, les vérifications effectuées sur les lieux ont notamment permis de constater la présence de différentes boissons alcoolisées, dont du pastis, faisant l’objet d’un procédé présumé de fabrication et/ou de reconditionnement. Ce qui les a amenés à saisir «environ 500 bouteilles de boissons, ainsi que des fûts, des cartons contenant des boissons et divers matériels utilisés dans le processus » au cours de l’intervention. « Des personnes ont également été interpellées pour les besoins de la procédure», indique la source. Après avoir remercié les populations pour leur vigilance et leur collaboration, la Police municipale les encourage «à poursuivre la dénonciation de tout fait ou comportement susceptible de porter atteinte à la sécurité, à la salubrité et à la santé publiques» au N° Vert : 80 00 11 03 ou bien au contact WhatsApp: 70 00 83 41 pour des messages uniquement. Par Wakat Séra L’article Ouagadougou: un réseau clandestin de fabrication et de reconditionnement de boissons alcoolisées démasqué est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .
